conventions.track: basic = content for ~2-4, on by default; advanced = raises and ~4-7 content, reachable only when the parent turns the advanced track on for that strand AND every id in `requires` is mastered.
conventions.params: Base parameters passed to the template. Ranges are [min, max] inclusive integers.
conventions.variants: Optional list of parameter overrides; the runner cycles them round by round (e.g. more / less / equal). A level is mastered only when its window includes every variant.
conventions.stage: Concrete-pictorial-abstract order. The runner starts at the first stage, moves on after 3 first-try wins in a row, and drops back one stage after 2 consecutive misses.
conventions.existing: Existing content-pack levels (content/packs/*.json) that become this level or its transfer pool.
conventions.age: Guide only, never a gate (all five council seats).
conventions.station: Space Map station the level launches from.

M.desc: At least 4 of the last 5 first committed responses correct without an answer-revealing hint, in each of 2 sessions on different days, including at least 1 transfer item (different representation or context).

M4.desc: M for long items (rover, tangram, rangoli, word builder): 3 of the last 4, in each of 2 sessions.

E.desc: M scored on the observation/evidence answer only; the prediction is never scored.

L.desc: M tracked separately per language (en, fr, fa); sentence audio played before answering routes evidence to listening, not reading.

R.desc: Rhythm: order and long/short/rest pattern correct within +/-35% of a beat (UNVERIFIED tolerance). Never a speed score.

X.desc: Exploration, unassessed. Visiting it never advances or steps back anything.

objective.en: Gives one object to each of 1-3 recipients, and tap-counts 1-3 objects once each.

levels.example: Give each of three astronauts one helmet.

objective.en: Counts 1-5 objects and chooses the matching total (dots or numeral).

levels.example: Count four moon rocks; choose the four-dot card.

objective.en: Recognises 1-4 objects without counting, across dice, line and scattered arrangements.

levels.example: Three lights glow, then the dome covers them; tap the three-dot card (peek again any time).

objective.en: Tells which group has more, fewer, or the same (to 5), even when spacing or object size differs.

levels.example: Four big stars spread out vs five small stars packed close: which has more?

objective.en: Counts 6-10 objects with one-to-one tapping and matches the total to a numeral.

levels.example: Count eight satellites; tap 8.

objective.en: Finds one more, one less, and adds or takes away 1-2 within 10 by hopping, with objects always available.

levels.example: Rocket on 4; one hop back. Where does it land? (the current '4 - 1' level)

levels.evidence: strong (Clements & Sarama Building Blocks, per Kimi)

objective.en: Recognises 5-10 as 'five and some more' on five-frames, ten-frames and dice pairs without counting one by one.

levels.example: A full row of five and two more: 'five and two, seven'.

levels.evidence: moderate (Singapore NEL/CPA, per Kimi and Sol)

objective.en: Splits and joins totals of 3-5 into two parts (including zero), then finds a hidden part.

levels.example: Five fuel pods; three are in the rocket. How many hid under the dome?

levels.evidence: moderate (soroban structure + rekenrek; Barner et al. 2016 is school-age)

objective.en: Shows any number 1-10 on a two-row bead frame using the five landmark, and shows how many more make ten.

levels.example: Slide beads to show 7: one full row and two. How many more make 10?

objective.en: Finds the missing part for totals 6-10 (missing addend), moving from pictures to numerals.

levels.example: 10 is 7 and ? (circles, then '7 + ? = 10').

objective.en: Builds and reads 11-19 as one full ten and some more, hearing 'ten and four' before the teen name.

levels.example: One full cabin and four more: 'ten and four, fourteen'.

objective.en: Follows an untimed 3-step string within 10 ('show 6, add 2, take 1'), with objects on demand.

levels.example: Show 6. Two more land. One flies away. How many now?

objective.en: Adds within 20 by completing ten first on a double ten-frame (8 + 5 = 8 + 2 + 3).

levels.example: 8 + 5: move 2 to fill the first cabin; 10 and 3 is 13.

objective.en: Solves spoken part-whole stories within 20 using a bar strip, finding either a part or the whole.

levels.example: 12 probes; 5 went to Mars. The bar shows 5 and a gap: how many went to the Moon?

objective.en: Matches circles, squares and triangles to identical outlines.

levels.example: Park the round pod in the round bay.

objective.en: Chooses the longer, shorter or taller of two objects standing on the same baseline.

levels.example: Which antenna is longer?

objective.en: Places an object in, on, under or beside a visible reference.

levels.example: Put the rover under the bridge.

objective.en: Tells heavier/lighter on a pan balance and fuller/emptier between two same-size containers.

levels.example: The balance tips: which moon rock is heavier? Which fuel tank is fuller?

objective.en: Finds a named circle, triangle, square or rectangle across size, rotation and non-typical forms.

levels.example: Find the triangle, even when its point faces sideways.

objective.en: Lines up three objects from shortest to longest (or smallest to biggest).

levels.example: Line up three rockets from shortest to tallest.

objective.en: Finds and places things on the left, in the middle, on the right and between, using real screen sides in every language.

levels.example: Put the satellite between the two moons.

levels.evidence: moderate (Davydov, Grade 1; adapted as play per Sol)

objective.en: Makes two paths or tanks equal by adding or removing, and says which needed more.

levels.example: Make the two rover tracks the same length.

objective.en: Fills a simple silhouette with 2-3 pieces (no rotation needed).

levels.example: Join two triangles into a square solar panel.

levels.evidence: moderate (Davydov; Sol: smaller units give larger counts)

objective.en: Measures with equal units end to end without gaps or overlaps, spots a flawed measurement, and sees smaller units give a bigger count.

levels.example: The landing strip is 6 tiles long. With half-size tiles, is it more or fewer?

objective.en: Matches spheres, cubes, cylinders and cones across different views and everyday objects.

levels.example: A planet is a sphere; the rocket nose is a cone.

levels.evidence: strong for spatial training (Uttal et al. 2013, per Kimi); cultural-form claims UNVERIFIED

objective.en: Fills a silhouette with 4-5 tangram pieces, rotating pieces by quarter turns; any valid solution counts.

levels.example: Build a rocket from five pieces; tap a piece to turn it.

objective.en: Completes the mirror half of a dot-grid picture across a vertical, then horizontal, line.

levels.example: Finish the butterfly nebula's other wing.

objective.en: Sorts 4 objects into 2 craters by kind.

levels.example: Stars in one crater, moons in the other.

objective.en: Sorts 5 objects into 2 groups by colour or by size.

levels.example: Big rocks here, small rocks there.

objective.en: Continues an AB pattern.

levels.example: Moon, star, moon, star, ...?

objective.en: Finds the one that does not belong among 4 (one feature differs).

levels.example: Three rockets and a moon: which is different?

objective.en: Plans 2-3 forward moves, then runs the rover to the sample.

levels.example: Three forwards to the blue rock.

objective.en: Extends AAB, ABB and ABC patterns.

levels.example: Rocket, rocket, moon, rocket, rocket, ...?

objective.en: Puts 3 pictured steps of a familiar procedure in order.

levels.example: Helmet on, climb in, blast off.

objective.en: Fills a gap inside AB/AAB/ABC patterns and finds the wrong car.

levels.example: Red, blue, yellow, red, ?, yellow.

objective.en: Plans a 3-4 move route with one turn; also drives step by step with direction buttons.

levels.example: Forward, turn left, forward to the base.

objective.en: Sorts 6 objects by two attributes at once into 4 craters.

levels.example: Red moons, blue moons, red stars, blue stars.

objective.en: Picks the odd one out and a picture of why; spots what changed between two scenes.

levels.example: Which pod is odd, and why: colour, stripes or size?

objective.en: Plans 5-6 moves around rocks, and predicts then fixes one wrong command.

levels.example: The rover will bump the rock: swap the left turn for a right turn.

objective.en: Continues patterns that grow by 1 or 2.

levels.example: 1 light, 2 lights, 3 lights, ...?

objective.en: Sorts pictures into the day sky or the night sky.

levels.example: Sun and rainbow go to day; Moon and stars go to night.

objective.en: Finds the Sun, Moon, a cloud, rain or snow in real photographs.

levels.example: Where is the rain?

objective.en: Sorts hot and cold things, including sourced facts such as Mercury near the Sun and icy Neptune.

levels.example: Hot cocoa and the Sun here; snowman and Neptune there.

objective.en: Chooses what a plant or animal needs (water, light, food) from concrete choices.

levels.example: The habitat plant is thirsty: water or a toy?

objective.en: Finds a named planet among 3-4 real images.

levels.example: Where is Saturn?

objective.en: Predicts, watches a verified test, and reports whether an object floated or sank.

levels.example: Wooden block: guess, drop, watch. What happened? (never 'heavy things sink')

objective.en: Predicts which side a shadow falls when a lamp moves, then reports what the shadow did.

levels.example: Lamp moves to the left: where is the rover's shadow now?

objective.en: Turns a globe with quarter-turn taps until a marked home faces the Sun (day) or away (night).

levels.example: Turn Earth until the home marker is in the dark.

objective.en: Sorts planets into rocky and gas giants, then stars, planets and moons by role.

levels.example: Jupiter is a gas giant; Mars is rocky.

objective.en: Orders a local tree through four seasons and spots what changed between two pictures.

levels.example: Blossom, green leaves, orange leaves, bare branches with snow.

objective.en: Sequences four simplified Moon landmarks and shows sunlight as what lights the Moon.

levels.example: New, first quarter, full, last quarter, then again. (never 'Earth's shadow')

objective.en: Chooses a comparison that changes one thing and says what the result showed.

levels.example: Same ice cubes, same trays, one in sun and one in shade: which melted first?

objective.en: Taps a familiar object among 2-3 pictures after hearing its name.

levels.example: Where is the comet?

objective.en: Follows a one-step spoken action with a familiar object.

levels.example: Put the astronaut in the rocket.

objective.en: Picks the picture for one of a pair of opposites (big/small, up/down, full/empty, fast/slow).

levels.example: The rocket goes up. Now tap the one going down.

objective.en: Follows a two-step instruction in order.

levels.example: Tap the rocket, then the Moon.

objective.en: Orders 3 pictures after hearing a short story.

levels.example: Hear the story, then put the three pictures in order.

objective.en: Taps once per syllable of a familiar word (tap count, not timing).

levels.example: Ju-pi-ter: three taps.

objective.en: Picks the picture that rhymes with a spoken word, using reviewed pairs per language.

levels.example: EN moon: spoon or star? (FR/FA use their own pairs)

objective.en: Matches pictures by the same first sound, without printed letters.

levels.example: Mmm-moon: Mars, Sun or star?

objective.en: Finds a named letter among 3-4 in the child's script (Persian isolated forms first).

levels.example: Where is M? / its Persian counterpart in the fa pack.

objective.en: Hears a taught sound and picks its letter from a small cumulative set; tracing is optional and never scored.

levels.example: Hear /s/; tap S, then trace it with big checkpoint taps if she wants.

objective.en: Blends 2-3 spoken sounds into a word and taps its picture.

levels.example: s-u-n: which picture?

objective.en: Builds short words from taught letter tiles after hearing them.

levels.example: Build 'sun' from four tiles.

objective.en: Reads a short fully decodable sentence and picks the matching scene.

levels.example: EN 'The cat sat.' once every letter in it is taught; fr/fa packs author their own texts.

strands.priority: build last (Astra defers it; Fable and Gemini include it)

objective.en: Plays along on the big drum with a slow steady beat (exploration, not scored).

levels.example: Boom, boom, boom, boom with the pulsar.

objective.en: Tells which of two sounds was louder or softer.

levels.example: Which planet drum was louder?

objective.en: Tells which of two beats was faster or slower.

levels.example: Fast rocket beat or slow drifting-asteroid beat?

objective.en: Taps back a 2-tap pattern.

levels.example: Ta ta: your turn.

objective.en: Tells which of two notes was higher or lower.

levels.example: Tiny satellite chime or big gas-giant rumble: which was higher?

objective.en: Taps back a 3-beat pattern with long and short sounds.

levels.example: Ta, ta-ti, ta.

objective.en: Tells whether a 3-note tune goes up or down.

levels.example: Rocket climbing (do-mi-sol) or landing (sol-mi-do)?

objective.en: Taps back 4 beats that include one silent beat.

levels.example: Ta, ta, (rest), ta.

objective.en: Plays back a 3-note tune on a 3-key planet xylophone.

levels.example: Mercury, Venus, Earth keys: play it back.

objective.en: Matches a heard AB or AAB rhythm to its pattern train.

levels.example: Long, short, long, short: which train shows it?

templates.interaction: tap beats or pictures; replay freely

templates.mechanic: Play along, compare two sounds, or hear a rhythm/tune and tap it back on a drum or 3-key xylophone.

space_map.role: Sun hub: parent gear, free play (Tap & Hear, Planet Song, Rocket Trip), never assessed

space_map.note: space topics; new sub-station orbiting Earth

placement.start: Parent sets a start level per strand in the parent gear by choosing an example the child can already do (no ages, no numbers shown to the child). Advanced track is a per-strand toggle.

probe.trigger: parent action or first visit to a station

visit.lookAhead: at most 1 item from the next level, only when 3 of the last 4 are first-try; counts toward advancing only

after2ConsecutiveMisses: drop one CPA stage / show counters
support.after3MissesInWindow: offer the prerequisite for the rest of this visit only; next visit resumes the same level

placement.neverErase: Mastered levels are never un-mastered; probe skips are 'placed', not 'done', so they do not add map moons.
placement.firstTry: misses === 0 AND no answer-revealing hint shown (replaying the prompt is fine)

generated.note: all number, music and most space/logic levels; seeded generator + deterministic answer/uniqueness checks

authored_shared.note: 12 science levels, space.9/.12/.13 (tangram, rangoli), logic.4/.7/.11 (math circle, sequences); one item set shared across locales, prompts translated and reviewed

authored_per_locale.note: language strand; authored independently per language, never translated

v1_volume.minimum_note: 10 distinct items for two 5-item mastery sessions + 3 reserved probe items
